muhammad.name: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
muhammad.summary: Seal of the prophets and messengers, Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib of the Banū Hāshim, of Quraysh.
muhammad.bio: He was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant and grew up an orphan; among his people he was known as the Truthful, the Trustworthy. He was sent at the age of forty, called to the oneness of God for twenty-three years, and then died in Madinah al-Munawwarah.
muhammad.context: He lived in a tribal environment in the Arabian Peninsula dominated by idol worship, and his message came with monotheism and the building of a new society based on justice and brotherhood.

companions.name: The Companions
companions.summary: Those who met the Prophet ﷺ as believers in him and died holding that faith.
companions.bio: The definition of a Companion according to the majority of hadith scholars: one who met the Prophet ﷺ as a believer in him and died as a Muslim. They carried the message, transmitted the Sunna and founded the state after him.
companions.context: They fall into different ranks: the foremost early believers, the emigrants to Abyssinia, the people of Badr, those who gave the Pledge of Riḍwān, and those who embraced Islam in the year of the Conquest.

makkah.name: Makkah al-Mukarramah
makkah.when: Birth and upbringing of the Prophet ﷺ
makkah.summary: Birthplace of the Prophet ﷺ, home of the revelation and seat of the Noble Kaʿba.
makkah.bio: A city in a valley without cultivation in the Hijaz, containing the Sacred House; it was a commercial and religious centre led by Quraysh.
makkah.context: The Prophet ﷺ spent fifty-three years there before the Hijra, and conquered it in 8 AH.

madinah.name: Madinah al-Munawwarah
madinah.summary: The city of the Hijra, capital of the first Islamic state and burial place of the Prophet ﷺ.
madinah.bio: It was called Yathrib and was inhabited by the Aws and the Khazraj and Jewish tribes. After the Hijra the Prophet ﷺ changed its name to Ṭayba and al-Madīna.
madinah.context: It contains the Prophet’s Mosque; the expeditions set out from it, and the Muslim community was built in it.

hira.name: Cave of Ḥirāʾ
hira.summary: The cave where the Prophet ﷺ used to worship and where the first revelation came.
hira.bio: A small cave on Jabal al-Nūr, about three miles from Makkah, where the Prophet ﷺ used to retreat for devotion for a number of nights.
hira.context: The first verses of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq were revealed in it.

kaaba.name: The Noble Kaʿba
kaaba.summary: The Sacred House whose foundations were raised by Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl, peace be upon them.
kaaba.bio: Quraysh rebuilt it about five years before the mission; the Prophet ﷺ took part in this and arbitrated in the placing of the Black Stone.
kaaba.context: The Prophet ﷺ cleansed it of idols on the day of the Conquest of Makkah.

taif.name: Ṭāʾif
taif.summary: The city the Prophet ﷺ went to in order to call its people, who rejected him.
taif.bio: The Prophet ﷺ went out to it with Zayd ibn Ḥāritha after the death of Abū Ṭālib and Khadīja; its foolish ones harmed him and threw stones at him.
taif.context: It is reported in the Ṣaḥīḥ that Jibrīl offered to bring the two mountains together upon them, and he said: “Rather, I hope that God will bring forth from their loins those who worship God alone.”

habasha.name: Abyssinia
habasha.summary: The land to which the first Muslims emigrated under the protection of the just Negus.
habasha.bio: The Prophet ﷺ said to the Muslims: “There is a king there with whom no one is wronged.” They stayed there secure in their religion.
habasha.context: Among the most prominent who emigrated there were ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, his wife Ruqayya, and Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib.

elephant.name: Year of the Elephant
elephant.summary: The attempt of Abraha the Abyssinian to destroy the Kaʿba and the destruction of his army.
elephant.bio: Abraha led an army including elephants to Makkah, and God sent upon it flocks of birds. In this year the Prophet ﷺ was born.
elephant.context: Sūrat al-Fīl mentions it, and the Arabs used it to date events.

birth.name: Birth of the Prophet ﷺ
birth.when: 12 Rabīʿ al-Awwal – Year of the Elephant
birth.summary: The birth of Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh in Makkah, an orphan.
birth.disputed: The day of the month is disputed: the best-known is 12 Rabīʿ al-Awwal; 2, 8 or 9 are also reported. Contemporary astronomers favour 9 Rabīʿ al-Awwal.
birth.bio: He was born after the death of his father ʿAbd Allāh, and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and then his uncle Abū Ṭālib took him in. He was put out to nurse among the Banū Saʿd with Ḥalīma al-Saʿdiyya.
birth.context: What is agreed upon is that he was born on a Monday in the Year of the Elephant.

marriage.name: Marriage to Khadīja
marriage.summary: The marriage of the Prophet ﷺ to Khadīja bint Khuwaylid when he was twenty-five.
marriage.disputed: Khadīja’s age at marriage: the best-known view is forty; others are reported.
marriage.bio: The Prophet ﷺ worked in her trade to al-Shām, she saw his trustworthiness and proposed marriage to him. She bore him his children except Ibrāhīm.
marriage.context: She was the first to believe in him and his support in the hardest years of the call.

revelation.name: The Revelation
revelation.summary: Jibrīl brought the first verses of the Qurʾān in the Cave of Ḥirāʾ: “Read in the name of your Lord who created.”
revelation.disputed: The day of the first revelation in Ramadan is disputed (17th, 21st or 24th); many consider the Night of Power most likely.
revelation.bio: The Prophet ﷺ was forty when Jibrīl came and embraced him and said: “Read.” He returned to Khadīja with his heart trembling; she reassured him and took him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal.
revelation.context: Then the revelation paused for a time, and Sūrat al-Muddaththir was revealed with the command to warn.

dawah.name: The Public Call
dawah.summary: After three years of secret preaching, God commanded His Prophet to proclaim the message openly.
dawah.bio: The Prophet ﷺ ascended Mount al-Ṣafā and called out to Quraysh, and the saying of the Most High was revealed (meaning): “And warn your closest kinsmen.”
dawah.context: After that the harm done by the polytheists to the Muslims intensified.

habasha_hijra.name: Migration to Abyssinia
habasha_hijra.summary: Muslims fled with their faith from the persecution of Quraysh to the Negus.
habasha_hijra.bio: The first group departed, about twelve men and four women, and larger groups followed them. Quraysh sent a delegation to the Negus, who sent them back.
habasha_hijra.context: The books of biography preserved the dialogue between Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and the Negus.

sorrow.name: Year of Sorrow
sorrow.summary: The deaths of Abū Ṭālib and then Khadīja, and the Prophet’s ﷺ journey to Ṭāʾif.
sorrow.bio: The Prophet ﷺ lost his protector and his wife within a short period, and the harm from Quraysh grew more intense.
sorrow.context: It was named thus by the biographers.

isra.name: The Night Journey and Ascension
isra.summary: The Prophet’s ﷺ night journey from the Sacred Mosque to al-Aqṣā, then his ascent through the heavens.
isra.disputed: That the journey took place is certain, but its date is disputed; no sound evidence supports the well-known 27th of Rajab.
isra.bio: The five prayers were made obligatory in it, and the Prophet ﷺ saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.
isra.context: The Qurʾān mentions it at the beginning of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ and in Sūrat al-Najm.

aqaba.name: The Two Pledges of ʿAqaba
aqaba.summary: A delegation of the Anṣār pledged to support and protect the Prophet ﷺ as they would protect their own women and children.
aqaba.bio: At the First ʿAqaba twelve gave the pledge, and at the Second seventy-three men and two women. The Prophet ﷺ sent Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr as a teacher.
aqaba.context: It directly paved the way for the Hijra to Madinah.

hijra.name: The Hijra to Madinah
hijra.summary: The Prophet ﷺ moved with Abū Bakr from Makkah to Madinah, the start of the Hijri calendar.
hijra.bio: The two left by night and hid in the Cave of Thawr for three days, then travelled with a guide to Qubāʾ and then Madinah. Its people received him with joy.
hijra.context: It was used for dating in the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him.

madina_state.name: Building the Islamic State
madina_state.summary: Building the Prophet’s Mosque, the brotherhood between Muhājirūn and Anṣār, and the writing of the Charter of Madinah.
madina_state.disputed: The Charter is reported by Ibn Isḥāq and others, but its wording and its compilation into a single document are debated among scholars.
madina_state.bio: The Prophet ﷺ began by building the mosque, then established brotherhood between the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, and regulated relations among the people of Madinah with a document known as the Ṣaḥīfa (Charter) of Madinah.
madina_state.context: These steps formed the nucleus of the community and the state.

badr.name: Battle of Badr
badr.summary: The first decisive battle between the Muslims and Quraysh, won by the Muslims.
badr.bio: The Prophet ﷺ went out with about three hundred and thirteen men and they faced about a thousand of Quraysh; God gave them victory despite their small numbers and equipment.
badr.context: The Qurʾān called it the Day of Criterion (Yawm al-Furqān).

uhud.name: Battle of Uḥud
uhud.summary: A battle at Mount Uḥud in which Ḥamza and a number of Companions were martyred.
uhud.bio: It began with victory for the Muslims, then the archers disobeyed the Prophet’s ﷺ command, and Khālid ibn al-Walīd circled around with the cavalry of Quraysh.
uhud.context: Sūrat Āl ʿImrān speaks about it.

khandaq.name: Battle of the Trench
khandaq.summary: The confederates allied to besiege Madinah, and the trench was dug on the advice of Salmān al-Fārisī.
khandaq.bio: The confederates besieged Madinah for about a month, and God sent upon them a wind and soldiers, and they departed disappointed.
khandaq.context: Verses of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb were revealed about it.

hudaybiyyah.name: Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya
hudaybiyyah.summary: A treaty between the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh to halt the war for ten years.
hudaybiyyah.bio: The Prophet ﷺ set out intending ʿumra and Quraysh prevented him, so they agreed to a truce on his returning the following year. The treaty seemed burdensome to some Companions, but God called it a victory.
hudaybiyyah.context: It was followed by the Pledge of Riḍwān under the tree.

fath.name: Conquest of Makkah
fath.summary: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah with ten thousand of his Companions and cleansed the Kaʿba of idols.
fath.bio: Quraysh broke the treaty, so the Prophet ﷺ marched on it; he entered humbly and pardoned its people, saying: “Go, for you are the released.”
fath.context: After it people entered the religion of God in crowds.

farewell.name: Farewell Pilgrimage
farewell.summary: The Prophet’s ﷺ only pilgrimage, in which he gave the comprehensive sermon of ʿArafa.
farewell.bio: He gave a sermon at ʿArafa affirming the sanctity of blood and property and the rights of women, and the saying of the Most High was revealed (meaning): “This day I have perfected your religion for you.”
farewell.context: More than a hundred thousand Companions were with him.

death.name: Death of the Prophet ﷺ
death.summary: The Prophet ﷺ passed to the Highest Companion in Madinah at the age of sixty-three.
death.disputed: The most widely held view is that he died on Monday 12 Rabīʿ al-Awwal; 2 Rabīʿ al-Awwal is also reported.
death.bio: He was ill for some days and commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer; he died in the house of ʿĀʾisha, may God be pleased with her, and was buried in it.
death.context: Abū Bakr took over the caliphate after him.

khadija.name: Khadīja bint Khuwaylid
khadija.summary: The first Mother of the Believers and the first to believe in the Prophet ﷺ.
khadija.bio: A Qurayshi businesswoman of wealth and nobility; the Prophet ﷺ married her and took no other wife while she lived. She supported the call with her wealth and her self.
khadija.context: She died three years before the Hijra, and the Prophet ﷺ used to mention her with loyalty.

abubakr.name: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq
abubakr.summary: Companion of the Prophet ﷺ in the cave and the first of the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
abubakr.bio: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Quḥāfa al-Taymī, the first man to accept Islam in the well-known report; he freed the oppressed and accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijra. He took on the caliphate after his death ﷺ.
abubakr.context: He fought the apostates and collected the Qurʾān into pages on the advice of ʿUmar.

umar.name: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
umar.summary: al-Fārūq, the second Rightly Guided Caliph; his conversion strengthened Islam.
umar.bio: From the Banū ʿAdī, he was known for firmness in the truth and for justice. He accepted Islam in Makkah and witnessed all the battles, and held the caliphate for ten years in which al-Shām, Iraq and Egypt were conquered.
umar.context: He established the Hijri calendar and set up the registers (dīwāns).

uthman.name: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān
uthman.summary: Dhū al-Nūrayn, the third Rightly Guided Caliph.
uthman.bio: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, Ruqayya and then Umm Kulthūm. He emigrated to Abyssinia and then Madinah, equipped the Army of Hardship, and unified the copies of the Qurʾān into a single codex.
uthman.context: He was martyred in the turmoil in 35 AH.

ali.name: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
ali.summary: Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, husband of Fāṭima and the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.
ali.bio: He grew up in the household of the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam young. He slept in his bed on the night of the Hijra and returned the trusts, and witnessed the battles except Tabūk.
ali.context: He was known for knowledge, courage and judgment.

aisha.name: ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr
aisha.summary: Mother of the Believers, among the Companions with the most narrations and jurisprudence.
aisha.bio: The Prophet ﷺ married her in Makkah and consummated the marriage in Madinah. She narrated more than two thousand hadiths, and senior Companions used to ask her.
aisha.context: The Prophet ﷺ died in her house and was buried in it.

bilal.name: Bilāl ibn Rabāḥ
bilal.summary: The first muezzin in Islam, known for his steadfastness under torture.
bilal.disputed: The year and place of his death are disputed among the biographical sources (Damascus or Aleppo).
bilal.bio: An Abyssinian slave of Umayya ibn Khalaf, tortured for his Islam, he said “One, One (Aḥad, Aḥad)”; Abū Bakr bought him and freed him.
bilal.context: He gave the call to prayer on the day of the Conquest of Makkah from atop the Kaʿba.

hamza.name: Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib
hamza.summary: Uncle of the Prophet ﷺ and Lion of God, the master of the martyrs.
hamza.bio: He accepted Islam in the second year of the mission and the Muslims were strengthened through him. He distinguished himself at Badr and was martyred at Uḥud.
hamza.context: Waḥshī ibn Ḥarb killed him at the command of Hind bint ʿUtba.

abutalib.name: Abū Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib
abutalib.summary: Uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, his guardian and protector against Quraysh.
abutalib.bio: He took the Prophet ﷺ in after his grandfather and protected him from the harm of Quraysh for ten years after the mission, but he died on the religion of his people.
abutalib.context: It is reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that he did not utter the declaration of faith at his death.

najashi.name: The Negus Aṣḥama
najashi.summary: The just king of Abyssinia who gave refuge to the emigrants.
najashi.bio: He listened to Sūrat Maryam from Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and wept, refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraysh, and accepted Islam.
najashi.context: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the funeral prayer for him in absentia when he died.

musab.name: Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr
musab.summary: The first ambassador in Islam, sent by the Prophet ﷺ to teach the people of Madinah.
musab.bio: A pampered young man of Makkah who gave up comfort for his religion. Many of the Anṣār accepted Islam at his hand, among them Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and Saʿd ibn Muʿādh.
musab.context: He carried the Muslims’ banner at Uḥud and was martyred.

salman.name: Salmān al-Fārisī
salman.summary: The seeker of truth from Persia and the adviser of the Trench.
salman.disputed: His age at death is very much disputed among the reports.
salman.bio: He travelled from Persia seeking the truth until he reached Madinah and accepted Islam. He proposed digging the trench.
salman.context: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Salmān is one of us, the people of the House.”

khalid.name: Khālid ibn al-Walīd
khalid.summary: The Drawn Sword of God, a great military commander.
khalid.bio: One of the horsemen of Quraysh who led the encirclement at Uḥud, then accepted Islam before the Conquest, witnessed Mūta and led armies after the Prophet ﷺ.
khalid.context: The Prophet ﷺ named him the Sword of God.

abdurrahman.name: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf
abdurrahman.summary: One of the ten promised Paradise, and the trustworthy merchant among the Companions.
abdurrahman.bio: He emigrated twice, and the Prophet ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ, but he refused his brother’s wealth and said: “Show me the market.”
abdurrahman.context: He gave a great fortune in charity in the way of God.
